section_summary: This section covers the postwar administrative reorganization of the Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Central Liaison Office between February 1948 and June 1949 under Allied Occupation. It details the initial abolition of the Central Liaison Office and redistribution of its liaison responsibilities to the Prime Minister's Office in 1948, followed by comprehensive 1949 reforms that streamlined the ministry into five bureaus, reincorporated the Liaison Bureau, and established the Foreign Service Training Institute under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Establishment Law. The documentation includes diplomatic despatches, SCAP directives, draft statutes, ministerial regulations, organizational comparison charts, and records on treaty preparations and diplomatic recruitment.

subfiles.about: Reports the abolition of the Central Liaison Office and outlines planned structural and personnel changes in the Foreign Ministry.
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports that effective February 1, 1948, the Central Liaison Office was abolished, with its duties shifted to the Prime Minister's Office and Cabinet Secretariat. The Foreign Ministry absorbed repatriation, records, and civil property responsibilities. He also details proposed bureau restructuring and high-level personnel changes, including the resignation of Vice Minister Okazaki.

subfiles.summary: Draft statute establishing the scope of responsibilities and powers of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. It defines the Minister's Secretariat and five internal bureaus (Political Affairs, Treaties, Research, Controls, and Liaison), the Foreign Service Training Institute, the Central Liaison Committee, and eleven local branch offices, taking effect June 1, 1949.
